description: A book scene and a public source support one useful, bounded wider resonance.

input.cue: The Caterpillar's calm questioning makes Alice's confusion feel like a test. Does that connect to anything outside the book?

tool_evidence.excerpt: The Caterpillar asks who Alice is. Alice says she hardly knows because she has changed several times and cannot explain herself.

tool_evidence.title: Existentialism
tool_evidence.excerpt: The source describes existentialist attention to how identity is made through situated choices rather than received as a complete, fixed definition.

criteria: Connects Alice's pressured self-explanation to the public source without claiming equivalence
Preserves the difference between a comic fictional exchange and a philosophical account
Frames the outside connection as an optional interpretive lens
forbidden_claims: Lewis Carroll was writing existentialist philosophy
The public source proves the only correct reading of the scene
